levers.method_note: HMRC direct effect of 1 point on the main rate of corporation tax: 3.6bn in 2026-27, 4bn by 2028-29 (HMRC-DE-2025-06). Low–high is an editorial ±10% because HMRC publishes a central figure only. HMRC includes taxpayers' own behavioural response where it models one, but no wider economic effects.

HMRC direct effect of 1p a litre on the main rate of fuel duty: 0.414bn in 2026-27, 0.397bn by 2028-29 (HMRC-DE-2025-06). Low–high is an editorial ±10% because HMRC publishes a central figure only. HMRC includes taxpayers' own behavioural response where it models one, but no wider economic effects. Derived, not published: HMRC's 1% petrol + diesel rows (240m) divided by 1% of a 57.95p/litre main rate, so 1p/litre = 1% x 100/57.95. 57.95p is the bulletin's current rate plus the pence its notes say the baseline adds back. HMRC also uprates the baseline rate by forecast RPI each April, so this overstates 1p by roughly cumulative RPI (a few % in year one, more later). Includes behavioural response; no economy-wide effects. Starting rate 52.95p a litre, in force since 2022-03-23 (GOV.UK). Already scheduled: 55.95p from 2027-01-01; 57.95p from 2027-03-01.
